finding: The page does not define the algorithm that assigns turbines to strings, orders turbines within each string, or locates/selects the offshore substation node.
evidence: The page defines a resulting edge set E but not how E is constructed. The upstream layout page supplies turbine coordinates only. ORBIT documents explicit grid and ring construction rules, including a substation coordinate.
model_consequence: Different valid radial trees produce different lengths, conductor allocations, installation sections, losses and costs; an independent implementer cannot reproduce L_horizontal.
recommendation: Adopt one deterministic screening topology algorithm and define its substation-location rule, tie-breaking, feasibility checks and returned section list. Detailed route optimisation can remain outside scope.

finding: Total pull-in and vertical cable length has no input or calculation, while L_array requires it.
evidence: The page explicitly states that no default is inserted until water depth and interface assumptions are defined and lists supply length as incomplete.
model_consequence: Complete supply length, cable mass, supply CAPEX and installation inventory cannot be calculated.
recommendation: Define a geometry-based pull-in length relationship or retain it as a scenario input with an explicit owner, units, counting rule and missing-input behaviour.

finding: The page owns infield-grid electrical performance but supplies no loss calculation or adopted loss input.
evidence: The model limitations state that electrical losses are unresolved. The shared energy methodology requires infield AC losses to be applied at component level. The cited ORBIT cable files already expose resistance, capacitance and inductance inputs.
model_consequence: Delivered electrical energy and LCOE are incomplete; applying zero loss would systematically favour architectures using the AC array network.
recommendation: Implement the minimum sufficient load-dependent segment loss model using the time-varying downstream power, selected conductor resistance, voltage and an explicit power-factor treatment. Keep detailed reactive and thermal studies as qualification checks or sensitivities.

finding: The 34-string base case cannot connect to the cited TenneT 2 GW reference platform with at most 28 indicated wind-farm/universal bays, and no compatible reference solution is selected.
evidence: The page correctly exposes the conflict. TenneT's 2024 presentation shows 4 x 6 offshore-wind-farm bays plus 4 universal bays and four 500 MW generation blocks.
model_consequence: The cable network, collection switchgear, platform inventory and installation case do not describe one physically closed reference architecture.
recommendation: Select and document a bay-compatible reference design before combining component costs. Preserve alternatives when rating uncertainty crosses the string-count threshold.

finding: The deterministic model requires one P_string value or an explicit branching rule, but the base case is given as the interval 64-66 MW.
evidence: The cited TenneT material supports a conservative 64 MW-per-cable basis; the page derives about 64.8 MW from 630 A, 66 kV and power factor 0.9, then carries a 64-66 MW range. For turbine ratings near a threshold, the interval changes floor(P_string/P_turb). The equation also needs a feasibility assertion when P_turb exceeds P_string.
model_consequence: Turbines per string and feeder count can be non-unique, causing discontinuous changes in length, bay count, accessories and cost.
recommendation: Use a conservative scalar for a base case or calculate and report both threshold outcomes. Define P_string selection, power factor/derating ownership and the P_turb <= P_string feasibility rule.

finding: No rule allocates conductor sizes to individual string segments even though segment loading, cable price and mass vary materially with downstream turbine count.
evidence: The page provides 185 mm2 and 630 mm2 ORBIT anchors and states that an optimised design uses multiple sizes. The installation worked example nevertheless applies the 630 mm2 mass to the entire infield inventory, while the supply model applies one blended EUR/m rate.
model_consequence: Supply CAPEX and vessel loading are not driven by the physical section inventory; installation and supply calculations can use mutually inconsistent cable definitions.
recommendation: At minimum, assign each segment the smallest screened conductor class that carries its downstream load, and return length, mass and cost by conductor class. Treat unmodelled thermal and protection checks as qualification gates.

finding: The 400 EUR2025/m base rate and 200-600 sensitivity are judgemental blends rather than a reproducible transformation from the routed conductor inventory, and the stated accessory boundary is not demonstrated for the ORBIT rates.
evidence: The ORBIT values normalise correctly to about 219 and 590 EUR2025/m. The Hollandse Kust Zuid comparator is about 174 EUR/m in 2019 nominal terms and includes design, testing, cable and accessories. It is not restated to EUR2025 before being used to frame the adopted EUR2025 assumption. ORBIT's cost_per_km files do not define joints and termination-material inclusions.
model_consequence: Material CAPEX may be biased by conductor mix and incompatible cost scopes; discrete accessory costs can be omitted or hidden inside an unsupported length rate.
recommendation: Use conductor-specific rates on a common price basis and document procurement scope. Model material accessories by count where evidence permits; otherwise label their omission or aggregate treatment explicitly.

finding: The 20% base route allowance and 5-20% sensitivity have no external evidence or site basis.
evidence: The cited internal Word document says that cables cannot cross and therefore adds 20% for diversion. Cable crossings are possible with engineered crossing arrangements, and the document gives no project data or derivation for 20%. The page appropriately warns not to double count routed geometry, but still adopts 20% as the base.
model_consequence: The assumption changes cable supply, mass and installation quantities by up to 20% without traceable support.
recommendation: Treat route allowance as a scenario input until route-specific evidence exists; use zero when coordinates are routed and use explicit crossing/protection quantities in the installation model.

finding: The adopted 2% of supply CAPEX per year and 1-3% range are not supported by the cited failure evidence.
evidence: SPARTA reports portfolio cable-outage occurrence and lost production; ELECTRODE reports combined repair cost and lost generation. The page correctly states that neither source provides array-only cash repair expenditure, but it nevertheless introduces the percentage without a separate basis.
model_consequence: Annual OPEX is a material LCOE input and scales with cable purchase price rather than failure exposure, repair scope or installed-system cost.
recommendation: Leave the value unresolved until a defensible top-down benchmark or event model is available, or document the percentage as an explicit decision with an evidenced calibration target and broad sensitivity.

finding: The 99.0% array-network availability factor has no derivation, citation or sensitivity range.
evidence: SPARTA supports that cable outages occur and provides portfolio statistics, but it does not directly justify a 99.0% array-only energy-equivalent multiplier. The page labels the value as aggregate but does not show why it is appropriate.
model_consequence: Annual energy changes directly by the factor, while radial topology and affected capacity are hidden; uncertainty is not propagated.
recommendation: Provide an evidence or calibration basis and sensitivity. Until then, classify 99.0% as an unresolved modelling decision rather than a supported input.

finding: The table presents 132 kV as a selectable sensitivity, but no 132 kV cable capacity, cost, mass, loss, switchgear or platform-interface model is defined.
evidence: The Carbon Trust source supports 132 kV as a future option and potential system savings, while the page limitation states that 132 kV is not optimised.
model_consequence: A model implementer cannot run the stated voltage sensitivity, and fixing 66 kV can bias designs with larger turbines or constrained feeder-bay counts.
recommendation: Either remove 132 kV from executable sensitivities and label it future scope, or add a complete 132 kV parameter and interface set before using it in comparisons.

finding: The cost owner for offshore 66 kV collection switchgear is ambiguous for the centralised-hydrogen architecture.
evidence: This page excludes offshore switchgear bays. The electrical overview assigns collection switchgear to the HVDC Converter Stations page, but that page is not used by centralised hydrogen. The electrolyser power-electronics page explicitly excludes upstream 66 kV switchgear.
model_consequence: Centralised-hydrogen CAPEX and equipment mass can omit the offshore collection switchgear or depend on an architecture-inapplicable page.
recommendation: Assign one canonical owner for common offshore AC collection switchgear and define whether its cost and mass scale by string, bay, generation block or platform.

finding: The ORBIT cable inputs are cited from the mutable dev branch rather than an immutable release or commit.
evidence: The reviewed files currently contain the reported current, cost and mass values, and the ORBIT changelog identifies them as 2024 USD updates. A future dev-branch change can make the page values no longer reproducible from the citation.
model_consequence: A reader may be unable to reconstruct the adopted input version later.
recommendation: Pin the ORBIT version and commit hash used by both cable-supply and installation pages and cite immutable file URLs.

finding: Several citations need a stable or more precise source statement even though the underlying claims are broadly supportable.
evidence: The TenneT 2015 URL was not retrievable during review; the Prysmian bibliography points to a withdrawn annual report although an approved 3 April 2020 version exists; IEC 63026 states rated voltage up to 60 kV with Um 72.5 kV, so the blanket phrase '66 kV-class' needs precise voltage-designation wording; the live DNV page now identifies edition 2025-12.
model_consequence: Evidence maintenance and standard-edition ambiguity weaken long-term traceability but do not currently change the screening calculation.
recommendation: Replace unstable or withdrawn links, cite exact document editions/pages, and state the cable voltage designation used when describing IEC scope.

finding: The two architectures use different delivered products and delivery points in the LCOE denominator: grid electricity versus hydrogen HHV at a backbone connection.
evidence: METH-002 defines electricity at the onshore grid and hydrogen on an HHV basis; ARCH-001 and ARCH-005 explicitly exclude storage, reconversion, distribution and end use beyond those unequal interfaces.
model_consequence: EUR/MWh values are not a like-for-like end-service comparison. Ranking the carriers can change with downstream conversion, storage, demand matching and connection costs.
recommendation: Choose the comparison purpose explicitly: either compare carrier-specific costs at separate interfaces without ranking them as equivalent, or extend both pathways to one common demand service and include every downstream cost and loss.
downstream_pages: ARCH-001; ARCH-002; ARCH-003; ARCH-004; ARCH-005; METH-006
resolution: Defined separate Tier 1 onshore electricity and hydrogen endpoints and units and prohibited equivalent end-use ranking; aligned all architecture labels.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: endpoint terms and units reconcile across six methodology and five architecture pages; full render passed.

finding: The expression LCOE = C1/Yield + C2/Capacity Factor + C3 is dimensionally undefined and groups monetary costs and energy losses in one additive term.
evidence: C1-C3 have no units or normalisation basis. Dividing a capacity-linked cost by a dimensionless capacity factor does not produce EUR/MWh without rated capacity and annual hours, while a conversion loss cannot be added directly to a monetary cost.
model_consequence: Readers can implement or interpret a relationship that is not dimensionally reproducible, obscuring the actual dependency between capacity-rated assets and delivered energy.
recommendation: Replace the expression with the auditable annual-cost equation and a separate delivered-energy equation. If a conceptual decomposition is retained, define each term so every addend has EUR/MWh units.
resolution: Removed the C1/C2/C3 expression and replaced it with dimensionally explicit capital-intensity and carrier-cost equations linked to annual cost and delivered energy.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: automated unit-basis checks and full render passed.

finding: The claimed lifecycle cost boundary includes common development, financing and decommissioning activities, but no page owns or parameterises several of those cost categories.
evidence: ARCH-001 says lifecycle activities are included and ARCH-002 to ARCH-004 retain common development and financing costs. ARCH-005 says those costs are represented elsewhere, but the repository has no canonical development-cost owner and installation pages explicitly exclude development, insurance, owner contingency and decommissioning.
model_consequence: The numerator cannot be closed consistently and omissions may differ by architecture if residual package factors are used elsewhere.
recommendation: Add a project-cost scope matrix with a canonical owner and treatment for development, engineering, insurance, construction finance, contingency, commissioning, decommissioning and any excluded categories. Do not call an item included until it has an owner or explicit zero/exclusion decision.
downstream_pages: ARCH-001; ARCH-002; ARCH-003; ARCH-004; ARCH-005; INST-001; INST-002; INST-003; INST-004
resolution: Added a canonical cost-scope matrix: component and installation owners are explicit; METH-003 owns shared fields and decommissioning; financing taxes and fees are explicitly excluded; unresolved required fields return not parameterized.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: ownership and missing-input behavior reconcile across methodology and architecture pages; full render passed.

finding: The 6.6% real WACC is an unsupported carried assumption and its tax, financing and architecture scope are not defined.
evidence: The page labels the value as a TODO. It does not state pre-tax versus post-tax treatment, whether the same financing applies to all carrier-specific assets, or a sensitivity range. Published cost-of-capital evidence is basis-sensitive.
model_consequence: WACC directly affects every annualised CAPEX term and may bias architectures with different capital intensity or asset risk.
recommendation: Select a documented real WACC convention with tax and financing scope, establish a base case and range, and test architecture-specific financing only if evidence supports the distinction.
resolution: COR-01B now identifies 6.6% as one provisional project-wide real assumption and explicitly excludes tax debt and construction-finance timing; the evidence basis and sensitivity range remain unresolved.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md confirms the scope and arithmetic; issue remains open pending evidence and sensitivity.

finding: The simple CRF treatment does not define how component replacements, different lifetimes, decommissioning and residual value enter annual cost.
evidence: The page explicitly says these items require discounted cash-flow terms but supplies no equation or timing convention. H2P-003 already states at least one stack replacement within the 25-year project and calculates replacement cost.
model_consequence: Annual cost and LCOE are incomplete and can materially misstate architectures with short-lived stacks or different replacement profiles.
recommendation: Define a real discounted-cash-flow annualisation equation with expenditure timing, replacement count, residual value and decommissioning treatment, then derive an equivalent annual cost on the common project basis.
resolution: Implemented the approved simplified alternative: explicit replacement counts within 25 years, zero residual value, decommissioning at 80% of offshore installation CAPEX and one lifecycle capital basis annualized by CRF without timing discounts.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: CRF and 25/10/5-year replacement cases reproduce; full render passed.

finding: Stack overplanting, pipeline pressure and pipeline selection are classified as scenario parameters on METH-004 but as optimisation variables on METH-005.
evidence: The two adjacent methodology pages assign the same quantities to mutually exclusive roles. The hydrogen infrastructure overview also says pressure, diameter and pipeline count are optimised jointly.
model_consequence: Implementers can hold a quantity fixed, sweep it externally or optimise it internally and obtain different design sets and reported optima.
recommendation: Create one canonical variable taxonomy. For each quantity define whether it is fixed, scenario-controlled, enumerated design variable or derived result; distinguish base-case sweeps from optimisation variables.
resolution: Published one taxonomy of user inputs fixed parameters derived quantities and outputs; overplanting pressure and pipeline class are deterministic user inputs and alternative cases are supplied externally.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: methodology pages and input register use the same classifications; full render passed.

finding: The workflow names input classes and outputs but does not specify an executable calculation sequence, time resolution, feasibility filtering or result-selection process.
evidence: No page-level algorithm connects wind time series, layout, component sizing, dispatch/curtailment, availability, annual energy, annual cost and comparison output. There is also no rule for failed or infeasible designs.
model_consequence: An independent implementer cannot reproduce the integrated model even when component equations are available.
recommendation: Document the model execution order and data contract, including temporal resolution, architecture branching, constraint checks, discrete equipment selection, infeasible-case handling, annual aggregation and output records.
resolution: Defined the eleven-step deterministic execution order from case validation through physical inventory energy availability cost annualization and reporting, with feasible infeasible and not-parameterized return states.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: required stages and return-state behavior pass source checks; full render passed.

finding: The optimisation problem is not mathematically specified: variable bounds and grids, constraints, objective evaluation and treatment of the cost-versus-density trade-off are absent.
evidence: The page states that variables are outcomes of system cost minimisation while also describing an areal-yield trade-off. It lists only some variables and provides no feasible ranges, discretisation, Pareto-dominance rule or tie-breaking convention.
model_consequence: Different searches can return different 'optimal' designs and can omit material discontinuities or infeasible regions.
recommendation: Define the design vector, scenario vector, bounds, discrete sets, feasibility constraints and output-selection rule. If cost and areal yield are co-objectives, report a non-dominated frontier rather than a single cost optimum unless the scenario supplies a constraint or weighting.
resolution: Removed the optimization claim and repurposed METH-005 as the deterministic input parameter derived-quantity and output contract; no internal search or result selection remains.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: published methodology contains only explicit no-optimizer statements and one-case return behavior; full render passed.

finding: The 2 GW HVDC block is introduced without a citation or the executable link-count and part-utilisation rule on the methodology page.
evidence: METH-005 states the 2 GW assumption without a source. ELEC-004 contains a ceiling-based link-count equation and the electrical pages cite the TenneT standard, but the optimisation page does not identify that canonical implementation or define how partially used final blocks are costed and dispatched.
model_consequence: The core discrete threshold can be implemented inconsistently or smoothed away in the optimisation.
recommendation: Link to the canonical sourced equation, define the exact rating and link-count rule, and state how partial final-block utilisation, curtailment and infeasibility are treated.
resolution: Classified 2 GW/link as a fixed sourced parameter cited at use and delegated link count partial utilization curtailment and feasibility to the linked canonical electrical pages.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: citation resolves and component links pass; full render passed.

finding: Availability has no canonical architecture mapping or combination rule and the shared table conflicts with component values.
evidence: METH-006 gives 98.5% for the electrolyser, while H2P-003 says stack availability is 99.5% throughout the study. The shared page does not say whether stack, BOP, power electronics and platform availability are bundled or multiplied, nor how partial-capacity states replace flat factors.
model_consequence: Annual delivered energy can be double-derated, under-derated or calculated differently by independent implementations.
recommendation: Define one availability ledger per architecture with owner, boundary, combination/replacement rule and explicit removal of flat factors when state-based models are used. Reconcile 98.5% versus 99.5%.
resolution: Added one side-by-side architecture ledger with component owners non-overlapping boundaries annual product rule redundancy treatment and embedded-derating exclusion; conflicting legacy values are explicitly not adopted.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: architecture ledger ownership and no-double-derating rules pass source checks; full render passed.

finding: Most shared availability factors are uncited assumptions with no derivation or sensitivity, including 100% pipeline availability.
evidence: The table supplies ten factors without citations. Component pages label several as legacy or modelling conventions; the infield cable pilot already records the unsupported 99.0% factor in ISS-0010.
model_consequence: Availability multiplies annual energy directly, and unsupported differences between electricity and hydrogen can predetermine the comparison.
recommendation: For each factor provide evidence or calibration, an architecture-specific scope and sensitivity. Retain 100% pipeline availability only as a transparent zero-outage scenario, not as a reliability result.
resolution: COR-01B removed unsupported legacy factors from the active ledger and defined their owners; required factors remain unresolved and 100% is permitted only as an explicit zero-outage scenario.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md confirms no unresolved factor is silently mapped to 1.0; issue remains open for component evidence and sensitivities.

finding: The hydrogen HHV value of 39.4 kWh/kg is technically correct but uncited at its point of introduction.
evidence: The page provides no citation. A U.S. DOE/NREL technical source reports HHV 39.42 kWh/kg and LHV 33.31 kWh/kg, confirming the rounded value.
model_consequence: The calculation is reproducible but does not meet the project's traceability rule for model-relevant numbers.
recommendation: Cite a stable primary or authoritative thermochemical source, state the reference condition and preserve the rounded 39.4 kWh/kg convention consistently.
resolution: Added the official DOE/NREL report to references.bib and cited 39.42 kWh/kg and its liquid-water HHV basis at the rounded 39.4 kWh/kg input.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01B.md: citation resolves and 39.4 kWh/kg conversion reproduces; full render passed.

finding: The one-platform centralised-hydrogen definition has no capacity, multiplicity or feasibility rule, and its material CAPEX and hosted-equipment mass are unresolved.
evidence: ARCH-003 fixes one physical platform while METH-004 permits varying turbine count. PLAT-001 requires platform count and hosted-equipment mass but explicitly has no adopted mass-to-CAPEX relationship and no closed mass inventory.
model_consequence: Centralised-hydrogen designs cannot be screened for platform feasibility or assigned a complete platform cost as farm capacity changes.
recommendation: Define the capacity range over which one integrated platform is the architecture, the rule when that range is exceeded, and the mass/cost interface required from component pages. Preserve platform-count discontinuities.

finding: The onshore hydrogen-backbone connection is included as a delivery interface but has no canonical component model or cost boundary.
evidence: ARCH-003, ARCH-004 and ARCH-005 link the connection to H2I-001, which describes compression and pipelines but does not define metering, pressure control, purification specification, connection equipment, tariff or CAPEX/OPEX. Downstream conditioning is only generically excluded.
model_consequence: Hydrogen delivery cost and technical acceptance at the stated endpoint may omit a material interface or overlap with pipeline/compressor scope.
recommendation: Create or assign a canonical connection-interface owner and define required pressure, purity, metering, valves, landfall/terminal equipment, CAPEX/OPEX and exclusions.

finding: The decentralised architecture has no owner for the export manifold and header-to-export connections.
evidence: H2I-002 explicitly excludes the export manifold and header-to-export connections from its length result. ARCH-004 and ARCH-005 include hydrogen collection and export pipeline but do not identify this connecting equipment as a component or assign its pressure loss, material, installation, cost or availability.
model_consequence: The physical network is not closed between the infield headers and export pipeline, so quantities, losses and costs are incomplete.
recommendation: Add the manifold/interface as an explicit component or extend one existing owner's boundary; define connection count, sizing, pressure loss, material/mass, installation and cost treatment.

finding: The scope-control matrix covers physical energy equipment well but does not map common lifecycle cost categories or unresolved non-equipment interfaces.
evidence: The page asserts that common development and financing scopes are represented elsewhere, yet supplies no owner rows. It also omits the decentralised export manifold and has only a generic owner for the hydrogen backbone connection.
model_consequence: The matrix cannot yet serve as a complete double-counting and omission control for the LCOE numerator.
recommendation: Extend the mapping with a separate economic-scope table covering common project costs, replacements, decommissioning and interface facilities, with an explicit owner or exclusion decision for each.

finding: The wind series cannot be independently reacquired from DOWA because extraction metadata are missing.
evidence: The legacy workbook has 87601 consecutive records but no grid point height source filename release/version timezone or direction convention and ends 72 hours before the stated official period.
model_consequence: All energy and wake results depend on an input whose site and operating basis cannot be verified or reproduced.
recommendation: Recover and record the exact DOWA extraction and period or select and freeze a new controlled source series with justification.

finding: The lower edge of each 30-degree sector is passed to the wake model as its representative direction.
evidence: The fitting script stores 0 for observations from 0 to below 30 degrees and PyWake consumes the stored labels. The representative centre is 15 degrees higher.
model_consequence: Wake alignment and the interaction with the fixed layout rotation are systematically shifted by 15 degrees.
recommendation: Use circular centre-labelled bins or add 15 degrees before wake evaluation and regenerate and validate all dependent yield outputs.

finding: The directional Weibull reduction and the two wind-speed integration grids have not been validated against the empirical hourly distribution or each other.
evidence: The page uses a 0.5 m/s PyWake grid and a 0.25 m/s midpoint hydrogen grid and itself requests an empirical-versus-fitted AEP check.
model_consequence: Distribution or quadrature error can be mistaken for an architecture energy difference.
recommendation: Report empirical-hourly versus Weibull AEP and convergence/reconciliation results with an acceptance tolerance before adoption.

finding: Farm area has no boundary or setback convention even though areal yield is a core objective.
evidence: The regular grid places coordinates on a bounding rectangle but does not state whether the modelled area includes half-spacing edge margins lease setbacks or excluded zones.
model_consequence: The same layout can be assigned different area and cost-density values and downstream route lengths.
recommendation: Define the functional area polygon and edge-margin convention and assert every turbine lies in the permitted area.

finding: Layouts below the stated minimum turbine spacing are only warned about rather than rejected.
evidence: The page identifies 3D as a screening minimum but allows the calculation and optimisation to continue and provides no evidence for that threshold.
model_consequence: The optimiser can select physically invalid high-density cases because they appear to minimise area or infrastructure.
recommendation: Adopt an evidenced screening constraint and return infeasible before wake cost and optimisation evaluation.

finding: The wake-model turbine curve and hub height are not the canonical turbine defined on TURB-002.
evidence: WIND-003 uses a synthetic 15 MW 236 m power/Ct table and 150 m hub height; TURB-002 defaults to 133 m at 236 m rotor diameter and does not own the synthetic wake curve.
model_consequence: Wake loss gross yield and structural/cost calculations describe different turbines.
recommendation: Create one controlled turbine-definition record for both pages including rotor hub height and power/Ct curves and regenerate dependent results.

finding: Layout orientation turbulence intensity and the PyWake configuration are not evidenced version-pinned or benchmarked.
evidence: The page uses 30 degrees TI 0.058 and TurboNOJ/PropagateDownwind settings without a source calibration or reported benchmark.
model_consequence: Outcome-driving wake loss can change with undocumented software versions and arbitrary fixed inputs.
recommendation: Document the source/role of each input pin the environment and benchmark or sensitivity-test the configuration including orientation.

finding: Architecture-specific turbine electrical equipment has no complete quantitative mass and cost ledger.
evidence: Converter switchgear protection internal cable and DC-link masses/costs are explicitly unresolved and the direct-DC retained equipment is not quantified.
model_consequence: Complete turbine mass CAPEX lifts foundation mass and decentralised architecture cost cannot be calculated.
recommendation: Define mutually exclusive conventional and direct-DC component ledgers with mass cost loss dimensions and owner for every retained removed or added item.

finding: The rule for applying architecture component substitutions to calibrated RNA cost is ambiguous.
evidence: The NREL RNA calibration can include commercial electrical supply scope while the page proposes removing/replacing named electrical components without stating whether deltas use raw or calibrated costs.
model_consequence: Electrical items can be double counted omitted or receive an unsupported calibration multiplier.
recommendation: Define the calibration boundary and apply architecture deltas with one explicit before/after-calibration equation and scope ledger.

finding: The length-only tower surrogate cannot respond to architecture-induced equipment mass or load changes.
evidence: The page acknowledges that lighter/heavier nacelle changes cannot feed back through the WISDEM tower regression.
model_consequence: Architecture foundation/tower mass credits may be omitted or claimed inconsistently.
recommendation: Either adopt a bounded load-responsive surrogate with supported inputs or explicitly grant no tower-mass credit and test a sensitivity.

finding: The monopile surrogate treats supported static mass and depth as the only drivers and its validation is confounded by changing turbine/load cases.
evidence: The three comparison designs vary rotor power loading and depth together; agreement does not isolate linear response to supported mass. Soil thrust dynamics and fatigue are omitted.
model_consequence: Architecture equipment-mass differences can receive unsupported linear foundation-mass credits.
recommendation: Choose a bounded surrogate with load/soil classes or adopt a no-credit rule for architecture mass deltas until stronger evidence is available.

finding: The USD per tonne cost is derived by pairing cost and mass from different reference designs without showing matched scope.
evidence: The NREL 250-350 USD2022/kW range is divided by a BVG 1850 t example with different design/source basis.
model_consequence: The resulting cost factor may mix fabrication scope turbine rating site and transition-piece treatment.
recommendation: Use a matched mass-and-cost source or retain a top-down per-kW range and make the unmatched conversion a sensitivity only.

finding: Transition-piece mass scour quantity and foundation lift/section records are missing or unowned.
evidence: The page calculates monopile mass and transition-piece cost only while installation and supported-mass consumers require physical quantities and lift geometry.
model_consequence: Foundation installation feasibility duration cost and complete structural inventory cannot be calculated.
recommendation: Assign scour ownership and emit transition-piece mass and all required foundation lift/section quantities with boundaries and sources.

finding: The direct-DC generator-to-PEM operating envelope cannot be verified with repository inputs.
evidence: Generator winding voltage and speed range converter limits and PEM envelopes over temperature pressure tolerance and ageing are absent.
model_consequence: The model cannot know whether the proposed topology can accept wind power without an extra conversion stage or how much is curtailed.
recommendation: Define a numerical capability-envelope interface and gate the architecture as conditional/infeasible until all inequalities and operating points pass.

finding: The retained direct-DC rectifier/up-chopper protection isolation and DC-link functions have no mass cost or loss model.
evidence: The page carefully retains the functions conceptually but neither it nor TURB-002 quantifies the corresponding equipment.
model_consequence: The decentralised architecture gains from removed equipment without booking the retained integration system.
recommendation: Close the shared TURB-002/H2P-002 ledger and show the net conventional-to-direct-DC mass cost and efficiency delta.

finding: The executable decentralised yield multiplies generator power by an undocumented 1.025 electric gain.
evidence: yield_params.yaml defines hydrogen_decentral_electric_gain=1.025 and aggregated_wind_power_curve.py multiplies wake-affected turbine power by it; the page specifies retained losses and no such factor.
model_consequence: The model can create stack-path power above the defined generator output and overstate decentralised hydrogen yield.
recommendation: Remove the multiplier or reformulate it as removal of a specifically defined baseline conversion loss while preserving one energy-conserving reference boundary.

finding: The stack polarisation/efficiency model is shown only as a figure and cannot be numerically reconstructed.
evidence: No table equation data file temperature pressure or interpolation rule is published while legacy code contains an undocumented cubic efficiency curve.
model_consequence: Hydrogen output operating point and direct-DC feasibility cannot be independently implemented or audited.
recommendation: Publish a machine-readable adopted curve with basis units valid range interpolation and conversion to HHV efficiency and reconcile it with code.

finding: Stack module rating and dispatch assumptions differ between the page and executable model.
evidence: The page repeatedly uses approximately 1 MW modules while generate_total_stack_efficiency_curve defaults to 2.5 MW and maximises efficiency over active-module counts with a 9.5% minimum.
model_consequence: Part-load efficiency minimum system load equipment count and switching behaviour are not reproducible from the documentation.
recommendation: Adopt one module rating and deterministic dispatch/switching rule including minimum load tie-breaking and hysteresis assumptions and align code.

finding: The degradation example is arithmetically wrong and its rate and EOL threshold are uncited.
evidence: Ten percent divided by 0.18 percent per 1000 FLH equals 55556 FLH not 58500; at 40 percent capacity factor this is about 15.9 years. The page supplies no source for either assumption.
model_consequence: Replacement timing hydrogen yield and lifecycle cost are misstated and unsupported.
recommendation: Correct the arithmetic cite or calibrate the degradation law and EOL criterion and make replacement conditional on accumulated operating state.

finding: The page describes optimisation-based stack replacement but the legacy implementation does not replace stacks or time replacement cash flows.
evidence: yield_calculation.py marks stack degradation TODO while the cost model contains no replacement event; only an average degradation multiplier is applied elsewhere.
model_consequence: A material lifecycle cost and production reset are absent despite the page claiming they are modelled.
recommendation: Implement a timed state/replacement ledger or explicitly adopt and validate a simpler equivalent method through the lifecycle cash-flow convention.

finding: The page presents incompatible 164 USD2020/kW 112 USD2020/kW and checked-later 100 EUR/kW stack costs without one adopted EUR2025 basis.

finding: A generic 0.6 exponent is applied to an aggregate 1 MW land-based BOP across multi-MW to GW offshore scales without train limits or redundancy.

finding: The documented constant BOP energy and 1 MW cost reference do not match the executable load-dependent loss curve and 15 MW cost reference.

finding: The DEA 2025 converter-station value is escalated a second time as though it were still a 2020 value.

finding: The cable page does not emit a complete segment-level physical inventory for installation.

finding: Converter cable and onshore electrical OPEX is absent on the pages or implemented only as unsupported legacy CAPEX percentages.

finding: The model has no selected PCC route grid-strength or acceptance scenario and no rule for infeasibility reinforcement or curtailment.

finding: Onshore converter loss and availability are numerically repeated on ELEC-005 despite ELEC-001 assigning their ownership to ELEC-003.

finding: The overview says one lay vessel can install multiple pipelines together while the canonical installation page permits one TCP per actual lay pass until contractor evidence proves another method.
evidence: H2I-001 uses shared laying as part of the optimisation rationale. H2I-005 and INST-003 explicitly state that simultaneous multi-pipeline installation must not be assumed. Legacy code divides pipeline count by a parallel factor of three.

recommendation: Use one physical TCP per provisional lay pass and model only shared mobilisation or programme costs with explicit evidence. Add a multi-pipe pass branch only after supplier and contractor qualification.

finding: The square continuous ladder proxy does not consume the rectangular rotated turbine coordinates produced by WIND-003 and smooths the physical rung-count discontinuity.
evidence: WIND-003 explicitly instructs infield models to consume its coordinates. H2I-002 instead uses sqrt(A) for every side and sqrt(N) rungs and recommends the 192 km continuous result over the 198 km twelve-rung physical result.

recommendation: Derive a deterministic ladder section list from the canonical coordinates and farm boundary. Preserve integer rows headers incomplete-row treatment and every connection; retain the continuous formula only as a validation comparator.

finding: No segment-by-segment flow pressure product-class or fault-state calculation establishes header capacity or the claimed two-path redundancy.
evidence: The page explicitly says header flow is higher that the current model does not check segments and that redundancy depends on valves isolation and remaining-path capacity. No valve or state topology is supplied.

finding: The page excludes risers tie-ins spool pieces routing slack and connection inventory while legacy code silently adds one sea-depth-plus-burial vertical length per turbine.

finding: The thermodynamic and real-gas property assumptions are not controlled consistently across the page figure builder legacy code and cited method.
evidence: The equation is an isentropic multistage relation with perfect intercooling but the page labels only a generic compressor efficiency. model_consequence: Energy curves and stage duties cannot be exactly reproduced and future property changes can silently alter the pressure optimum.
recommendation: State isentropic efficiency perfect intercooling suction/intercooler temperature and discharge-temperature checks. Select one average-property method pin CoolProp and use the same tested function for page figures and the executable model.

finding: The compressor cost equation omits its numerical reference power and cost currency price year transformation and non-overlapping offshore scope.

finding: One unbounded compressor power-law is applied to both turbine and farm scale without technology train-rating redundancy or turndown steps.
evidence: The cited source distinguishes large high-flow pipeline compressors from small high-ratio units sets a 16000 kW maximum large-compressor rating and assumes multiple units above it. The page acknowledges multiple central trains but still costs one farm-level compressor.

recommendation: Adopt architecture-specific compressor types and bounded train packages with maximum rating count spare philosophy turndown and discrete scaling; withhold comparison outside the evidence range.

finding: Compressor OPEX is 3 percent of CAPEX on the page 2 percent in legacy code and neither matches the cited source scope.
evidence: The source separates labour and electricity and uses 4 percent of TIC for fixed O&M plus insurance tax and licensing percentages. The page supplies no derivation for 3 percent and hydrogen_params.yaml uses 2 percent.
model_consequence: Lifecycle cost is not reproducible and maintenance or insurance scope can be omitted or double counted.
recommendation: Define a non-overlapping offshore compressor OPEX ledger for planned maintenance labour spares fault repair and other project costs; retain unresolved terms as TODOs and align page and code.

finding: The compressor page provides no train mass footprint dimensions or lift inventory for platform turbine and installation models.
evidence: H2I-003 supplies motor power and cost only. PLAT-001 and turbine/foundation pages require supported mass while installation pages require transport and lift modules.
model_consequence: Platform and turbine feasibility structural cost and installation cannot close and distributed compression receives no physical penalty.
recommendation: For each selected train/package return mass footprint envelope module count largest lift and architecture-specific support/interface requirements with source or explicit unresolved status.

finding: The implemented gas-flow relation is not the cited General Flow Equation and has no benchmark or velocity qualification.
evidence: Transition Accelerator uses flow proportional to sqrt(p_in^2-p_out^2) with absolute pressures. The page/code use linear delta-p with density at one average pressure and a Fanning Colebrook rearrangement. No derivation comparison Reynolds-regime or erosional/max-velocity check is reported.
model_consequence: Capacity error can change the ceiling-based pipeline count and selected pressure/diameter design especially near a discrete threshold.
recommendation: Implement the cited compressible gas-flow equation or provide and benchmark a rigorous alternative against it over every candidate. Add absolute-pressure Reynolds velocity and limiting-condition assertions.

finding: The 66 bar pipeline outlet mixes a Dutch network design maximum with an operating receipt condition and does not distinguish gauge from absolute pressure.
evidence: Hynetwork specifies 66.2 bar(g) design/maximum operating pressure and a temporary 30-50 bar(g) operating regime. The cited gas equation requires absolute pressure but the page and code pass 66 bar directly and provide no injection differential or terminal pressure-control rule.
model_consequence: Pipeline capacity and compression can be miscalculated and delivery may not satisfy the actual backbone interface without onshore control or recompression.
recommendation: Define a connection scenario with required operating receipt range minimum differential gauge-to-absolute conversion pressure control and recompression behavior; use design pressure only for product qualification.

finding: No named hydrogen-qualified TCP product defines true internal diameter pressure/temperature/life limits fittings linear mass reel length or installation envelope.
evidence: The 8 inch limit comes from the internal model and is treated as internal diameter. Public supplier material describes up to 7.5 inch internal diameter for 8 inch NPS and generic offshore capability but does not qualify the selected hydrogen design point. INST-003 therefore leaves TCP installation unparameterized.
model_consequence: Hydraulic capacity material quantity vessel selection connections permeation and feasibility cannot be tied to one physical product and capacity may be overstated.
recommendation: Use discrete named or bounded product classes with internal/outer diameter rated pressure temperature service life hydrogen qualification mass bend radius reel length fittings and installation gate. Reject unqualified candidates.

finding: The confidential pipeline cost model is not independently reproducible and its disclosed method description and fit quality are inadequate.
evidence: The page calls the surface interpolation but local code uses a global bilinear least-squares regression whose coefficients are intentionally untracked. A controlled check against quote points gives about 19 percent mean absolute percentage error and about 51 percent maximum error. Price year currency quote scope and residual validation are absent.
model_consequence: Material CAPEX and the selected architecture depend on an opaque relation with material approximation error and no public audit path.
recommendation: Adopt a publishable evidenced cost basis or a governed confidential-input process with version checksum scope price basis fit diagnostics uncertainty and a public validation/fallback range. Do not report a single auditable result from unavailable coefficients.

finding: Material cost varies smoothly with operating inlet pressure instead of selecting a discrete pipe rated-pressure class at or above design pressure.
evidence: Supplier points represent diameter/pressure options but the model evaluates I(D,p_in) continuously. Product reinforcement qualification and cost change by manufactured class and design margin rather than every operating bar.
model_consequence: The optimiser can buy fractionally rated pipe erase product-class thresholds and understate cost or use an infeasible construction.
recommendation: Enumerate qualified diameter and rated-pressure classes use operating pressure only in hydraulics and select the least class meeting design pressure including margin and external-load criteria.

finding: The 0.5 percent of material CAPEX annual pipeline OPEX has no cited derivation or defined inspection maintenance repair and replacement scope.
evidence: The value is listed as an adopted assumption and repeated in legacy parameters without evidence. Installation and availability pages separately discuss repair and outage states but no shared cost boundary exists.
model_consequence: Lifecycle pipeline cost can be biased and fault repair can be omitted or counted twice.
recommendation: Define planned inspection maintenance and fault-repair scopes with evidence or sensitivities and link repair events to the availability/install-vessel ledger. Leave unsupported cost unresolved.

finding: The offshore-installation overview links only the cable and pipeline page and does not route readers to the turbine/foundation or platform/substation calculations.
evidence: The overview names all asset classes but contains only one direct detail-page link.

finding: The turbine campaign has no effective site-occupation input and neither campaign has a coherent named vessel/spread record linking logistics limits task times and commercial rate.
evidence: The parameter table marks turbine site time TODO and payload/SWL as named-vessel inputs while the shown rate speed and logistics anchors come from different generic and project examples.

finding: The seven-day ORBIT mobilisation input is used as combined mobilisation and demobilisation time.

finding: The provisional 400000 USD2024/day WTIV rate is not matched to the page's self-shuttling no-feeder campaign configuration or a complete-spread commercial boundary.
evidence: The cited ORBIT introduction is a hypothetical example configured with two feeder vessels. The page excludes feeder logistics and uses the WTIV rate for self-shuttling foundation and turbine campaigns while payload SWL and inclusion scope remain unresolved.

recommendation: Adopt one physically and commercially coherent campaign configuration per spread and document vessel support craft crew fuel overhead mobilisation standby and port inclusions before using the rate.

finding: A payload result of zero sets per load reaches ceil(N/k) and causes division by zero instead of an infeasible campaign state.
evidence: k_payload is floor(M_use/m_set) and k is its minimum with the reference limit; no assertion requires k at least one before N_load=ceil(N/k).
model_consequence: An undersized vessel produces an implementation failure or undefined result rather than a transparent class-change requirement.
recommendation: Assert positive inputs and return infeasible whenever k_payload or the adopted k is below one before calculating loads.

finding: Scour port infrastructure feeder logistics ordinary mitigation commissioning and exceptional foundation work are excluded without a complete downstream owner or aggregate exceptional-cost interface.
evidence: The page correctly says excluded activities are not zero but supplies no cost term output contract or owner for several scopes; METH-002 already identifies lifecycle categories without owners and TURB-003 has no scour quantity.
model_consequence: Total installed CAPEX can omit material project scopes or corrections may later double count them.
recommendation: Create an exclusion/ownership ledger and explicit exceptional-scope output with quantity rate or unresolved status for every excluded activity.

finding: Lay production time uses horizontal route pass-km and omits slack and vertical product that are included in physical supply length and vessel loading.

finding: The lay duration includes initial outbound transit and reload round trips but no final site-to-port transit.

finding: The ORBIT cable-vessel operating rate does not demonstrate the complete all-in lay-spread inclusions required by the cost boundary.

finding: Burial and survey productivity and rates demobilisation weather port routing exceptional quantities and complete cable/TCP campaign definitions are unresolved.

finding: Platform installation lacks jacket pile and topside module records and does not screen pile lifting handling or transport feasibility.

finding: All three complete-spread rates mobilisation cost jacket/topside logistics and hook-up duration required for platform installation CAPEX are unresolved.

finding: A CVOW duration stated per complete topside is applied as 2.5 days for every arbitrary topside-module lift.

finding: Platform hook-up and commissioning are not reconciled with cable pull-in termination and final connection owned by INST-003.

finding: The methodology overview describes six child pages but provides no direct links to them.

finding: The About page overstates independent reproducibility of confidential inputs and understates the site's public evidence base.
evidence: The site actively cites 88 bibliography keys beyond the working Word documents while several reviewed models including the confidential TCP cost relation cannot be reconstructed without unavailable coefficients raw points or controlled files.
model_consequence: A reader can mistake controlled-internal reproducibility for public independent reproduction and misunderstand which results are auditable.
recommendation: State separate public and controlled-internal reproducibility levels link the evidence policy and describe the current model as incomplete where material confidential or unresolved inputs block independent results.
resolution: Rewrote About to distinguish public from controlled-internal reproducibility, state current development readiness, disclose confidential-evidence limits and link the evidence catalog.
validation_evidence: review/correction-validation/COR-01A.md: source checks and full site render passed.

finding: The sidebar completion percentages are undefined and conflict materially with calculation readiness and open findings.
evidence: Fourteen blocked pages display completion of 80 percent or more and ARCH-003 and ARCH-004 display 100 percent despite blockers. The progress script labels the values percent complete and no published legend distinguishes editorial completion from model readiness.
model_consequence: Readers can interpret polished prose as an executable validated model and may rely on blocked calculations or architecture claims.
recommendation: Define completion semantics and publish model readiness/evidence status separately or replace the percentage with controlled statuses linked to unresolved inputs and validation.
resolution: Replaced published completion percentages with controlled model-readiness badges sourced from QMD front matter; sections inherit the least-ready calculation child and About publishes the legend.
